paragraphs: Friend, think about WHERE this fight happens. Jesus has just said His betrayer is at the table, and the disciples start arguing about who is the greatest. I think that's the most human thing in the whole chapter. Jesus doesn't scold them, He just shows them a different way: "the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves" (Luke 22:26).

Then He says, "I am among you as one who serves" (Luke 22:27). The One who has every right to be on top is the One holding the towel. So the baker's question is not "How do I get ahead?" It's "Who can I serve today?" And here's the good part: He still promises a kingdom, because His Father bestowed one on Him (Luke 22:29). Serving doesn't cost you your place with Him.

Now look at Peter. Jesus tells him, "I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail," and adds, "when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers" (Luke 22:32). Notice He says WHEN, not IF. Peter says he's ready for prison and death, and I've made some big promises to my oven too, so I get it. But the lesson is that Jesus knows our weak spots and prays for us anyway. Hold on to that, baker, because this story is not over.
